title: Site24x7 products, plans, and add-ons for a small recommendation model
vendor: Site24x7, a ManageEngine product from Zoho Corporation

instructions_for_small_models.audience: A small model such as Qwen2.5 or Llama 3.2 answering 'which Site24x7 plan and add-ons should this buyer purchase?'
read_first: retrieval_chunks where id is how_to_choose or do_not_mix_legacy
the one plan chunk and the addon chunks you might select
license chunks only for the resource types in the question

caveats: List prices from Site24x7 public pages on 2026-10-21. Tax extra. Confirm at checkout.

procedure: Read the buyer's resources and turn them into counts: websites, browser transactions, servers/VMs, APM instances, database hosts, network devices (then components using the network rules), log GB and retention days, RUM page views, synthetic runs per month, customer accounts, status-page components and subscribers, domains to scan, or monthly cloud bill.

Pick the family with families[].choose_when. Never mix a website plan with servers. Never sell MSP to a single company. Never sell Infrastructure Professional if they need included RUM; sell All-in-one Professional at the same price.

If they need anomaly detection, event correlation, infrastructure events, NCM firmware vulnerability, NCM compliance, or video RCA, the plan must be infra_enterprise, aio_enterprise, or msp_enterprise. Those are not add-ons. The price is 'starts at'. Tell them the list starting price and that a quote is required. Do not invent how many servers are included.
Otherwise take the cheapest plan in the family whose included numbers cover every count. Use annual_billing_per_month.usd as the price you quote first, then mention month_to_month.usd.

If the included numbers are short, price the add-on packs that the plan lists under addons_allowed. Use only packs whose applies_to_addon_groups intersect that list. You may buy several of the same pack. Pick the cheapest combination that meets the gap. Compare that total with the next plan up. If the next plan is cheaper or within a few dollars, prefer the higher plan because it includes more features and support.
Lite's add-on menu is closed. If they need a pack Lite does not sell, recommend Professional (or All-in-one Professional) instead of stacking imaginary Lite packs.
Enterprise add-on prices are the ent_* packs, not the pro_* packs. Web Uptime can only take uptime-monitor packs. Web Perf takes synthetic combos and Web Perf RUM packs, not the uptime-only packs.
If two answers tie on price, prefer the one with fewer add-ons. If Infrastructure Professional and All-in-one Professional tie, prefer All-in-one Professional.

Hourly billing is only for the listed cloud/server/APM types, only on Lite/Professional (professional hourly rates) or Enterprise (enterprise hourly rates), and only when hours_per_day * hourly_rate * 30 is cheaper than a full license for that extra resource.

Say that prices were read from Site24x7's public pages and pricing script on 2026-10-21, are list prices in the currency asked (default USD), exclude tax, and that volume discounts exist via sales@site24x7.com or US +1 408 352 9117.

Do not recommend legacy STARTER, PRO, CLASSIC, ELITE, ENTERPRISE, or legacy MSP unless the user says they are already on that pack. If they are, do not migrate them in your head; compare their current pack's included monitors with the current plan that covers the same monitors and show both prices.
If a number is null or a caveat says it is unpublished, say it is not published. Do not fill it from the legacy comparison page.
hard_rules: Never invent a price, a quota, or an add-on pack that is not in this file.
Never apply a Professional add-on price to an Enterprise plan, or a Web Uptime add-on to Web Perf.
Never sell AIOps as an add-on.
If Enterprise included counts are null, say they are not published and the price starts at the listed amount.

Quote USD unless the user names gbp, eur, aud, or inr. Those four are official list prices in price_per_month, not a conversion you should calculate. INR is not USD times 95 even though the script contains INR_BASE_RATE 95.
Prefer annual_billing_per_month. Mention that paying month to month costs month_to_month.
Current plans use a 10% annual discount. The FAQ states this directly.
Taxes are extra. Volume discounts are not published; send large deals to sales@site24x7.com or US +1 408 352 9117.
A 30-day full trial exists and does not need a credit card.

Prefer add-on packs with shown_on_pricing_page_card true. Use a pack marked false only when no shown pack can cover the gap, and say that pack is in the official price script but not printed on the current card.
When a worked example in this file matches the question, use its arithmetic. Do not recompute a different pack mix for that same need.

families.name: Website Monitoring
families.choose_when: Only public websites, APIs, DNS, SSL, ping, ports, and optionally real-browser transactions and RUM. No servers, no cloud VMs, no APM instances, no network devices.

families.name: Infrastructure Monitoring
families.choose_when: Servers, cloud, network, and APM, and the buyer does not need included RUM. Same prices as All-in-one.

families.name: All-in-one Monitoring
families.choose_when: Servers plus the digital-experience pieces (especially RUM). Professional includes 100K RUM page views at the same price as Infrastructure Professional, so prefer this family when RUM is in scope or might be.

families.name: Managed Service Providers
families.choose_when: The buyer monitors other customers' environments from one MSP portal, or needs more than one customer account. A single company should not buy MSP.

families.name: StatusIQ
families.choose_when: Status pages only, or more status pages than the monitoring plan includes.

families.name: Digital Risk Analyzer
families.choose_when: External domain risk, attack surface, port and vulnerability assessment. Not uptime monitoring.

families.name: CloudSpend
families.choose_when: The buyer wants cloud-bill visibility and optimization, priced from the cloud bill, not from monitor counts.

products.name: Website and internet-service monitoring
products.covers: HTTP(S), REST, SOAP, WebSocket, DNS, NTP, FTP, SMTP, ping, TCP port, SSL/TLS and domain expiry, defacement, mail delivery, FTP transfer.

products.name: Synthetic / real-browser monitoring
products.covers: Web Transaction (Browser) and Web Page Speed (Browser). Licensed as advanced monitors or as synthetic runs.

products.name: Real user monitoring
products.covers: Browser page views, SPA, geography, JS errors, sessions, session replay on higher comparisons, mobile RUM as a separate add-on.

products.name: Server monitoring
products.covers: Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, OS X, agentless HP/IBM/Solaris/SNMP/WMI. Host license. 25 or 50 included processes depending on plan.

products.name: Public cloud monitoring
products.covers: AWS, Azure, GCP. VMs and EC2/Compute are host licenses. Most other cloud services are basic licenses. OCI is marketed; the pricing FAQ's license list is AWS, Azure, and GCP.

products.name: Kubernetes and containers
products.covers: Cluster is a basic monitor. Node is a host. First 10 containers per host included; then host licenses per 10 more Docker containers, or the $0.25 per container starting price.

products.name: Virtualization
products.covers: VMware, Nutanix, Hyper-V. Host licenses for clusters, hosts, and VMs. vCenter free.

products.name: Network monitoring
products.covers: SNMP devices, 10,000+ templates, Layer 2, topology, traps, NetFlow, NCM, IP SLA, Meraki, wireless, storage. Component licenses.

products.name: Application performance monitoring
products.covers: Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, PHP, Ruby on Rails. Instance is an advanced license. Key transaction is a basic license. Application object is free.

products.name: Log management
products.covers: Ingestion by GB, retention 7 to 90 days, search, dashboards, alerts.

products.name: AIOps
products.covers: Anomaly detection, event correlation, forecasting, outlier and capacity features as marked on the feature table. Anomaly detection and event correlation are sold inside Enterprise and MSP Enterprise, not as a cheap add-on.

products.name: Status pages
products.covers: Included counts on monitoring plans, plus the StatusIQ product.

products.name: MSP multi-customer portal
products.covers: Customer accounts, license caps, shared pools.

products.name: On-premise poller
products.covers: Monitor inside a firewall. Counts of pollers: Lite 1, Professional and MSP 10, Enterprise and MSP Enterprise 50. High availability of the poller is supported. Poller check frequency is fixed at 5 minutes.

products.name: Digital Risk Analyzer
products.covers: External domain risk and vulnerability assessment.

plans.best_for: Full-stack monitoring plus AIOps. Same starting price as Infrastructure Enterprise. Prefer this over infra_enterprise when the buyer also wants RUM, synthetics, and APM in the same subscription.
plans.not_for: Workloads that fit All-in-one Professional and do not need AIOps.

plans.name: MSP

price.currency_note: Figures are the per-month list price. annual_billing_per_month is what you pay each month on a yearly commitment (about 10% below month-to-month). month_to_month is the price if you pay monthly.

plans.best_for: A managed service provider or a team that must monitor several customer accounts from one portal, within a modest included license pool.
plans.not_for: A single company monitoring only its own stack (use Website, Infrastructure, or All-in-one). Not for AIOps (use MSP Enterprise).
licensing_notes: Nine customers are included. More customers need the customer add-on at the MSP add-on price.
The MSP can cap licenses per customer or let customers share one pool.
If monitors beyond the included pool are required, buy the MSP add-ons (same professional-tier pack prices) rather than promising the base plan will stretch.

hourly_billing.label: Hourly billing on Lite and Professional
hourly_billing.when_to_recommend: Resources that are monitored only part of the day, especially auto-scaled cloud VMs. Compare hourly cost with a full host or advanced license before recommending it.

professional_breakeven_hours_per_day.host_vs_unit_price_2_50: A full host at the published $2.50 per VM starting price costs the same as hourly at about 13.9 hours per day (2.50 / (0.006 * 30)). Under about 14 hours/day, hourly is cheaper than one host license. This comparison is for capacity BEYOND monitors already included in the plan.

hourly_billing.faq_example: Professional plan: an EC2 instance monitored 6 hours a day for 30 days costs 6 * 0.006 * 30 = $1.08. Two such instances cost $1.80, which the FAQ compares with a $2 host monitor.

hourly_billing.label: Hourly billing on Enterprise
hourly_billing.when_to_recommend: Same idea as Professional hourly, but only on an Enterprise subscription, and only for capacity beyond the unpublished Enterprise inclusion. The Enterprise base price already starts at $625 per month when billed annually.

apm_notes: The APM application is a free monitor. Instances are advanced. Key transactions are basic.
An APM host add-on exists in the FAQ: one add-on covers 25 APM instances on the same host. Its price is not in the public add-on script. Do not invent a price. Say to confirm with sales.
Trace cap stated in the FAQ: 30 traces per minute per application. Feature table says sampling is 30 traces/min on Lite and Professional.

FAQ also says trace retention of 30 days, while the feature table says span retention of 7 days (Lite/Professional) or 15 days (Enterprise). Quote the feature table for the plan and mention the FAQ's 30-day sentence as a conflicting statement, not as a promise.
license_rules.synthetic_choice: A browser monitor can burn one advanced license (and then poll on the plan's location and frequency schedule) OR burn synthetic runs (10,000 runs is the small pack). If there are many browser monitors or many locations, runs are often cheaper and the advanced licenses stay free for APM and databases. One transaction execution equals one synthetic run.

legacy_packs_do_not_recommend_for_new_bu.warning: DO NOT recommend these packs for a new buyer. The current pricing page sells Web Uptime, Web Perf, Enterprise Plus Web, Lite, Professional, Enterprise, MSP, and MSP Enterprise. These older packs remain in pricing1.js and on https://www.site24x7.com/packs-comparison.html. Their price-field names are inverted versus the new plans: in the script, legacy `.monthly` is the lower advertised per-month figure (what packs-comparison calls Pricing/month) and legacy `.annual` is the higher figure. For new plans it is the opposite: `.annual` is the yearly-commitment per-month price and `.monthly` is month-to-month. Mixing the two catalogs is the most common way to recommend the wrong product.

Legacy ENTERPRISE at $449 is not current Enterprise, which starts at $625 when billed annually.
Legacy MSP at $45 is not current MSP at $54 when billed annually.

Legacy WEB UPTIME at $10 on the comparison page is close to current Web Uptime month-to-month ($10) but the current plan card includes 25 websites, 32 locations, and 3 status pages. Use the current plan record, not the legacy column.
